title: Password hashing: bcrypt, scrypt and Argon2

videos.script: Sooner or later, somebody copies a database they should never have seen. A backup left in the wrong place is enough. {{leak}} What they find in the users table decides what happens next. If it holds the passwords, every account is theirs at once. {{table}} So you will not store a password. You will store something that can check one and cannot give it back. {{hash}} And you will make that check slow on purpose. You measure it on your own machine. A fast hash answers a million times a second. A password hash answers a few dozen times. {{rates}} Then you meet the three built for the job: bcrypt, scrypt and Argon2. Each one writes down everything it needs to check a password later, and you learn to read it. {{strings}} At the end the shelf gets accounts. Passwords stored with Argon2, checked at login, and upgraded when the settings change. {{shelf}}
